# nuthatch nest on arbitrum-one

A self-hosted blockchain index. Query it locally; there is no third-party API.

## Contracts
- `oracle` = 0x1cb555359319a94280acf85372ac2323aae2f5fd

## Tables (one per contract event)
- `oracle__new_ownership` - NewOwnership(address,address) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, from, to)
- `oracle__new_pending_ownership` - NewPendingOwnership(address,address) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, from, to)
- `oracle__oracle_set` - OracleSet(uint256,address) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, index, oracle)
- `oracle__oracle_vote` - OracleVote(bytes32,bool,uint256,uint256) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, subgraphDeploymentID, deny, oracleIndex, timestamp)
- `oracle__vote_time_limit_set` - VoteTimeLimitSet(uint256) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, voteTimeLimit)

## Live HTTP API (run `nuthatch dev`)
- `GET /`                    index status
- `GET /tables`              every table with its columns
- `GET /table/{name}?limit=N` recent rows of one table (hot + sealed)
- `GET /entity/{id}`         one row by id (`{block:012}-{logindex:06}`)
- `GET /sql?q=SELECT...`     read-only SQL; each table is a view named `{alias}__{event}`
- `GET /balances?limit=N`    top holder balances (when an ERC-20 Transfer table is present)
- `GET /balance/{address}`   one address's derived balance

## MCP (for coding agents)
Run `nuthatch mcp` (stdio) to expose tools: status, schema, tables, table, sql, entity,
balance, top_balances. Fully offline against the local instance; nothing phones home.
